facts.text: The repository integrates ROS 2 Humble, Gazebo Fortress, PyTorch and Stable Baselines3 with a Gymnasium interface, and simulates the Rover Zero, Clearpath Husky and Leo Rover platforms.
The README launches the Rover Zero simulation with ros2 launch roverrobotics_gazebo 4wd_rover_gazebo.launch.py.
RoverEnv is a gym.Env subclass documented as a custom environment that follows the Gymnasium interface.

The RoverEnv constructor defaults length to 2000, scan_topic to /scan, imu_topic to /imu/data, cmd_vel_topic to /cmd_vel, world_n to inspect, lidar_points to 32 and max_lidar_range to 12.0; these are constructor defaults, not device limits.
RoverEnv publishes geometry_msgs/Twist on cmd_vel and subscribes to LaserScan on scan_topic, Imu on imu_topic, PoseArray on /rover/pose_array and Odometry on /odometry/wheels.
The action space is a Box with low [-1.0, -pi] and high [1.0, pi], one speed and one relative heading value.
The observation space is a Dict of lidar (32 values from 0 to 12.0), pose (3 values), imu (3 angle values from -pi to pi), target (distance 0 to 100 and angle) and velocities (2 values).

step reads action[0] as speed and action[1] as a relative heading command, adds it to current_yaw, passes the result through heading_controller, and publishes linear.x = speed and angular.z = the controller output.
step increments _step, sets done when _step >= _length, and returns (observation, reward, done, False, info).
get_observation returns the lidar data, rover position, pitch/roll/yaw, target distance and relative angle, and linear/angular velocities.

reset calls super().reset(seed=seed), draws the start position and target with the module-level numpy random generator, sends an ign service set_pose command through subprocess, spins the node 100 times, sleeps for 1.0 s and returns (observation, {}).
close destroys the ROS node and shuts down rclpy.

determinism.notes: the fake's reset(seed=...) creates a local random.Random and its step rule is deterministic; the upstream reset calls super().reset(seed=seed) but draws the start pose and target from the module-level numpy generator, so the same seed is not known to repeat an upstream run

fidelity.engine: analytic:ROS-free kinematic stand-in for Gazebo Fortress
gaps: the fake is a ROS-free kinematic stand-in: it runs no rclpy node, ROS 2 graph, Gazebo Fortress physics, contacts, sensors, plugins or wall-clock loop, and no ign service reset
the upstream reset waits for 100 spin_once calls and time.sleep(1.0) after its ign service request; the fake resets immediately, so it does not model that latency
the upstream step waits for a fresh LaserScan while the fake applies its placeholder kinematic displacement immediately; one tick is one control transition with timestep_ms 0, not a physics step
the lidar array is a fixed 32-value placeholder; the real length is the constructor's lidar_points default of 32 and is configurable, and the upstream callback downsamples a LaserScan
the fake's reward is a simple progress term and its done flag only counts steps; it does not model the upstream collision, flip, stuck, out-of-bounds and goal logic in task_reward()
the fake's start pose, target, lidar reading and per-tick displacement are placeholder test data, not calibrated values, and its trajectories were not compared with a Gazebo run
the fake returns Python lists and floats; the upstream callbacks produce numpy arrays
no rendering and no snapshot/restore: the upstream class has no get_state()/set_state() pair and render() is a no-op
the action space is copied from the upstream Box and the observation space from the upstream Dict, but the dynamics behind them are not

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: For the declared analytic fake, the software latch fences subsequent step/reset calls. It does not pause Gazebo, does not publish a zero Twist on /cmd_vel, and does not stop a mobile base subscribed to that topic.
